todays_goal: Use a short oral-first repair for negative possession.

lessons.subject: french
lessons.previous_learning: Day 16 written check was 3/4; the remaining error was using des after pas.
lessons.course_context: Very short targeted repair rather than another full worksheet.
learning_objectives: Use de/d' after pas in negative possession.
Produce the pattern orally before writing.
lessons.why_it_matters: The pattern needs to become automatic so French can move forward.

vocabulary.definition: saying that someone does not have something

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: one small fix today. After pas in a possession sentence, use de or d'. Say it first, then write it.

exit_ticket.prompt: Say five new negative-possession sentences correctly.
exit_ticket.answer: Use ne/n' + avoir + pas + de/d' + noun.

lessons.voice_prompt: Oral first. Keep it fast. If he uses un/une/des after pas, point only to the noun phrase and ask what changes after pas. Use whiteboard circles/cross-outs for a different example.
